headline: Law requires the VA to provide lifelong health care, job training, and payments to certain veterans' children born with spina bifida or other birth defects.
what_it_does: The law requires the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to give covered children health care, job training, and monthly money benefits for their whole lives, no matter their age or whether they are married. It creates an advisory council on care and benefits for these children. It also sets up VA care teams that must reach out to each child at least every 180 days. In addition, two VA branches must sign an agreement to work together to help these children.

who_it_affects.group: Children of Vietnam veterans, and of veterans with certain service in Korea or Thailand, who were born with spina bifida
who_it_affects.how: They get VA health care, job training, and money benefits for life, plus regular check-ins from a VA care team.

who_it_affects.group: Children of women Vietnam veterans born with certain birth defects
who_it_affects.how: They get the same lifelong VA health care, job training, and money benefits, plus regular outreach.
The VA must form an advisory council and care teams, report to Congress a list of conditions that will trigger outreach, and contact children quickly when such a condition is found.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted October 6, 2023; the summary does not give specific start dates for each requirement.
